answer_text:
Let

\[
S(t)=f(4t)+f(2t)+f(t)+f\!\left(\frac t2\right)+f\!\left(\frac t4\right)+\cdots
\]

for \(t\neq 0\). The given condition says

\[
\frac{S(t)}{t}=64,
\]

so

\[
S(t)=64t \qquad (t\neq 0).
\]

Now evaluate \(S(t/2)\):

\[
S\!\left(\frac t2\right)
=
f(2t)+f(t)+f\!\left(\frac t2\right)+f\!\left(\frac t4\right)+\cdots
=
64\left(\frac t2\right)
=
32t.
\]

Subtracting \(S(t/2)\) from \(S(t)\) cancels the tail, leaving

\[
S(t)-S\!\left(\frac t2\right)=f(4t).
\]

Thus

\[
f(4t)=64t-32t=32t.
\]

Let \(x=4t\), so \(t=x/4\). For every \(x\neq 0\),

\[
f(x)=32\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)=8x.
\]

Since \(f(0)=0\), this also holds at \(x=0\). Therefore

\[
f(x)=8x
\]

for all \(x\). Hence

\[
f'(0)=\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{f(x)-f(0)}{x-0}
=\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{8x}{x}
=8.
\]

\[
\boxed{8}
\]
